clue.text: Words from lady of 21, ace seen mixing with folk: what innocent death, woe!

indicators.note: the letters of 'ace seen' are stirred together with the rest of the clue's closing words, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody quotes a lady, then a jumbled lament about folk, innocence, death and woe.
explanation.walkthrough: The 31 letters of the fodder rearrange into the whole quotation across 1, 24 and 27. The lady of 21 is the Queen Mother (Elizabeth Bowes-Lyon, of Glamis), who said this after Buckingham Palace was bombed in 1940; the East End is the poor, heavily bombed part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous remark attributed to Queen Elizabeth, later Queen Mother, after the palace was hit during the Blitz.

clue.text: Frantic protest over murderer being strung up

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the next

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: in a down answer, stringing something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Cain, the Biblical first murderer

explanation.surface: Someone is frenzied by a protest against a killer being hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoniac as an adjective means frenzied as if possessed by a demon, so frantic.

clue.text: Second best? Call it a day

parts.note: top as an adjective means best

explanation.surface: Coming second rather than first, an athlete decides to retire.
explanation.definitionFit: To call it a day is to cease doing something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Where the lady of 21 stood indeed!

definitions.meaning: the Queen Mother stood beside her husband King George VI
an old-fashioned exclamation of emphasis or surprise

explanation.walkthrough: The lady of 21 is Elizabeth Bowes-Lyon of Glamis, wife of George VI, so she stood by George.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild oath of surprise, and literally beside her royal husband named George.

clue.text: Tough TV lass mangled a man noted for scoring

indicators.note: something mangled is twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough television actress is hurt, it seems, in some accident.
explanation.walkthrough: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets; 'noted' plays on musical notes, and scoring means writing a score.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes scores, and Holst is a famous example of one.

clue.text: Perhaps talc, not women's, covering bloke — something scented

indicators.note: the shortened powder wraps around the next piece
the women's letter is left out of the talc word

parts.note: talc is an example of powder
W is the abbreviation for women
a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: Talcum powder without a feminine scent is dusted over a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not women's' leaves PODER, which by 'covering' wraps the bloke; talc tempts as the definition, but the scented thing is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomander is a ball of perfumed substances carried or hung to give off fragrance.

clue.text: Shiny thing shown by one of five Kent kids?

parts.note: Kent is in south-east England, abbreviated SE
a quin is one of quintuplets, five children born together

explanation.surface: Something sparkly appears on one of a set of quintuplets from Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' reinforces that the five are children; Kent is a county in the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequin is a small shiny disc sewn onto clothing for sparkle.

clue.text: Here nun intended to get drunk — time for lady of 21 to come on the scene

definitions.text: time for lady of 21 to come on the scene

indicators.note: being drunk leaves things in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun here planned to go on a drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Mother was born in that year (August 1900).
explanation.definitionFit: The year of her birth, when she first appeared in the world.

clue.text: Deliveries for second person to receive? The setter's done his bit!

definitions.text: Deliveries for second person to receive?
definitions.meaning: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so overs sent to 'you', the second person
a phrase handing responsibility to someone else, here the solver

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six deliveries; read as 'overs to you', the phrase becomes balls aimed at the second person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase hands the next move to the listener, as the setter does to the solver.

clue.text: Daggers when honour is given to deceiver, not half!

parts.note: OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

indicators.note: only half of the deceiver word is kept, the front part

parts.note: a liar deceives

explanation.surface: Someone sneers when a cheat is decorated, with a pun on 'not half!' meaning 'absolutely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger-shaped marks used in printing, plural of obelus.

clue.text: Shout of joy from little band coming in

indicators.note: the band goes inside the word for little

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
a hoop is a band, as round a barrel

explanation.surface: A cheer goes up as a small band marches in.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoopee is an exclamation of delight, a cry of joy.

clue.text: Dishonour brought by a duke breaking ceasefire

indicators.note: the duke pieces break into the ceasefire word

parts.note: a truce is a ceasefire

explanation.surface: A nobleman disgraces himself by violating an armistice.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce is to slander, damaging someone's honour, so a verb synonym.

clue.text: Cold joint may be one of those things served at meal time

definitions.text: may be one of those things served at meal time

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Cold meat on the bone might be dished up at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips, fried potatoes, are commonly served with a meal.

clue.text: Destiny of region occupied by noted characters

indicators.note: the region word holds the notes inside it

parts.note: a province is a region
D and E are musical notes, characters for notes

explanation.surface: Fate decided by a territory filled with famous people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted characters' looks like famous people but means letters that are names of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence is fate or divine guidance, close to destiny.

clue.text: Item of clothing shows audacity, leading to endless row

indicators.note: the first piece goes before the second

parts.note: neck is British slang for cheek, audacity

indicators.note: the last letter of the row word is dropped

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A bold garment choice starts an unending argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Row as in a quarrel is the false path; it is a row of seats, TIER, losing its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is a tie worn round the neck, an item of clothing.

clue.text: A gathering of wet leaves?

parts.note: tea leaves soaked in hot water, and a social gathering where such brew is served

explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon social event where an infusion of leaves is drunk.

clue.text: Have relation. possibly parent, to protect one

indicators.note: the rearranged parent wraps around one, protecting it
the letters of parent may be arranged some other way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mother or father may have a link, defending a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain is to relate or belong to something.

clue.text: Man or woman is kept outside hospital department — such may be waiting for doctor

definitions.text: such may be waiting for doctor

parts.note: Pat is a name used by both men and women

indicators.note: the word is stays outside, around the department

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

explanation.surface: Someone is barred from a hospital ward while others wait.
explanation.definitionFit: People queuing in a surgery waiting room are the doctor's sick clients.

clue.text: Girl's going round incapacitated in walks

indicators.note: the girl's name surrounds the next piece

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name, with possessive S
lame means disabled in the leg

explanation.surface: A girl walks around while hurt on a promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a tree-lined public promenade, a Spanish word for a walk.

clue.text: Attacks on lass out of order — unruly thug to be locked up

indicators.note: the rearranged thug goes inside the rearranged lass
lass in a disordered arrangement
thug with its letters running wild

explanation.surface: A ruffian attacks a girl and is jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges lass to SLAS; 'unruly' and 'to be locked up' scramble thug and jail it inside. The 'on' that opens the surface is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Onslaughts are fierce assaults, a plural synonym for attacks.

clue.text: Fuss when the first half goes the wrong way? It's fine

indicators.text: when the first half goes the wrong way
indicators.note: only the front three letters of the fuss word are turned round

parts.note: bustle is busy fuss

explanation.surface: A football team's fuss when it plays badly in the first half.
explanation.walkthrough: BUS, the first half of BUSTLE, is turned to SUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtle can mean fine as in delicate or finely drawn distinctions.

clue.text: Castle may be beautiful and alluring sitting atop island

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: glam is short for glamorous

explanation.surface: A lovely fortress perched above an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamis Castle in Scotland was the Queen Mother's childhood home.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamis Castle is a Scottish castle, family seat of the Bowes-Lyons.

clue.text: An objection when the last becomes first — it's forbidden

indicators.note: the final letter of the phrase moves to the front

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone objects when the rule changes and the last are first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, meaning forbidden.

clue.text: King by a British lake establishing mystical tradition

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Bala is the largest natural lake in Wales

explanation.surface: A king by a lake in Britain founds a mystic order.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabbala is Jewish mystical teaching handed down through tradition.

Fellow compiler got rid of makeshift place

definitions.meaning: The pseudonym of another Guardian crossword setter
past tense of to cast off or discard
a rough hut or lean-to structure

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the first refers to another Guardian setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague's setter name, a verb for discarded, and a simple hut.
